scale_basis: X = layout.json extent_m.x 48 m (Z = X*9/16 = 27.0), at true 1:1 hero-nest scale. Checked with the hero oak crown, drawn about 16.8 x 16 m (a mature oak), and its two upper limbs of about 7-8 m. VERTICAL DATUM: y = 0 is the top surface of the surrounding canopy, not the ground. The wood floor is about 20 m below (inferred) and outside this asset. Y = 6 m covers the crown rising 4 m above the canopy plus the air above the nest.
inferred_items: vertical datum at canopy top; ground about 20 m below (off-asset)
nest at the Bible 0.6 m across on the top fork at 2.9 m above datum, although the plan draws it about 3.5 m across
hero crown foliage as one soft ellipsoid 16 x 3.2 x 15 m, top at 2.7 m

upper limbs as two horizontal boxes at 3.4 m, rotated by yaw along the drawn limb lines (the overlay footprint ignores yaw); Bible gives three limbs, and the plan and layout.json show two, so two are modelled
surrounding canopy crowns are not modelled as geometry: they are the datum surface itself
units: metres; xy = normalised plan position (x right = east, y down = south = +Z); elevation_m = centre height above the canopy datum (host loader convention); yaw in radians

objects.note: leaf mass; Alice's neck passes through it at neck_gap (a torn gap, soft)
flat twig platform; the CGI Pigeon crouches, rises and beats its wings here

zones: none at ground level: this is an aerial scene. The Pigeon flies and perches on the nest and limbs. Alice's head and neck rise through neck_gap (xy 0.53, 0.62) and stand free above the crown.
